title: ExecutionReport
description: Structured return value from every execution-style workflow. Consumed by Opus post-run for cross-wave merges, progress YAML updates, plan-completion artifact, and Mode D escalation handling.

status.description: 'complete': all waves finished, all reviewers approved. 'blocked': a Mode D boundary was hit — Opus must run that phase interactively. 'needs_opus': reviewer escalation unresolved, budget exhausted, or a human-assigned (HITL) task gates the next wave — Opus must adjudicate.

reason.description: Present when status is 'blocked' or 'needs_opus'. Indicates the specific cause. 'hitl_required': the wave's agent work + reviewer gates completed but one or more human-assigned tasks must be signed off before advancing (see hitl_tasks). 'gate_failure': the reviewer gate DID NOT RUN — the reviewer returned no structured verdict (died after retries, or was skipped), so the scope is unreviewed rather than rejected. Distinct from 'reviewer_unresolved' on purpose, because the next action differs: a gate failure needs the reviewer re-dispatched (or an explicit operator override), NOT a fix cycle — there is no finding to act on, and fixing blind then re-reviewing unchanged code is how a phantom rejection burns a budget (authoring-spec §8b). 'scope_exceeds_single_pass' / 'spike_required' / 'plan_only' / 'plan_structure_failed' are autopilot-lane reasons (auto-feature workflow): respectively, the planned work exceeds single-pass capacity and needs full planning; unresolved research unknowns require a SPIKE/exploration first; planning ran with plan_only=true and awaits a go-ahead to execute; or the plan-structuring stage failed and Opus must read the plan artifact on disk. 'wrong_branch': the session working tree was NOT on the assigned run_branch, so agent commits would have landed off the branch the run may merge from — the PR/review/squash gates would have been bypassed silently. Detected pre-dispatch (nothing committed) or after a fix cycle moved HEAD. 'nothing_on_run_branch': the run finished with ZERO commits on the run branch since branch_base — every past-tense claim in the completion report is unproven, and this is never reported as 'complete'. 'cross_repo_target' / 'cross_repo_unverified': the graph targeted a different repo than the session, or could not be confirmed to match. 'invalid_graph': the ExecutionGraph failed validation before any agent spawned. 'post_verify_failed': the autopilot Phase-4 adversarial claims-vs-code pass found a confirmed critical/high defect, or produced no verdicts at all (unverified, not passed).

blocked_phase.description: When status is 'blocked', the id of the phase that triggered the Mode D boundary.

hitl_tasks.description: Present when reason is 'hitl_required'. The pending human-assigned tasks gating progression. Opus coordinates the human review (future: external task-tracker / intent-tree review request), then relaunches with these tasks marked complete / trimmed.

phase.description: Phase id the HITL task belongs to.

assigned_to.description: The human assignee (non-agent), e.g. a username.

prompt.description: What the human is asked to validate / sign off.

report.description: Per-wave results in execution order. Partial — may contain only completed waves if the run was interrupted.

autopilot.description: Present only on returns from the auto-feature (autopilot) workflow. Carries the classification + the durable plan artifact location so Opus can act on escalations or merge on success. Other execution workflows omit this field.

tier.description: Tier the planner classified the request into.

wave_count.description: Sequential dependency depth of the planned ExecutionGraph.

plan_artifact_path.description: Repo-relative path to the durable plan/contract artifact the planner wrote. Survives escalation so full planning gets a head start.

execution_target.description: Which engine the autopilot dispatched to (or 'none' when it escalated before executing).

escalation_recommendation.description: Human-readable next-step recommendation when the feasibility gate escalated.

blockers.description: Structured reasons the run halted, each with a concrete next action. Emitted by every non-complete engine return; previously absent from this schema even though the engines have always returned it.

run_placement.description: Where this run's work actually landed, and how to re-find it if the SHA moves. Present on EVERY outcome including 'complete' — provenance that appears only on failure is provenance consumers learn to ignore. Exists because a bare commit_sha cannot distinguish 'rebased away' from 'never existed': `git show <sha>` keeps working locally while the object survives gc, so a stale SHA reads as live right up until a fresh clone or CI resolves nothing. Consumers copying commit_sha forward (plan commit_refs, IntentTree nodes, delivery reports) should carry patch_id too.

run_branch.description: The branch the run was assigned. null when the caller did not name one.

base_sha.description: The pre-run checkpoint every diff and commit range was computed against.

current_branch.description: The branch the working tree was on when the report was assembled.

commit_count.description: Commits on the run branch since base_sha. 0 means nothing durable was produced.

head_sha.description: HEAD at report-assembly time, re-resolved after any fix cycle rather than captured at commit time.

patch_id.description: `git patch-id --stable` over base_sha..HEAD. Survives rebase, so it re-finds the work when commit_sha no longer resolves.

parent_tip_at_start.description: Parent-branch tip when the run began.

parent_tip_at_report.description: Parent-branch tip when the report was written.

parent_moved.description: True when the parent branch advanced mid-run (so a rebase may have changed commit_sha). null when either tip is unknown — never false on absent evidence.

verify_findings.description: Autopilot Phase-4 adversarial verify findings. Advisory when status stays complete; the cause when reason is post_verify_failed.

graph_errors.description: ExecutionGraph validation errors when reason is invalid_graph.

wave.description: Wave id matching the ExecutionGraph wave.

phase.description: Phase id matching the ExecutionGraph phase.

fix_cycles.description: Number of fix-loop iterations consumed. 0 means reviewer approved on first pass.

escalate.description: True when fix_cycles reached the maximum and verdict.approved is still false. Triggers needs_opus status at wave level.

files_touched.description: Union of files_affected across completed tasks in this phase. Used by Opus to scope worktree merge.

hitl_gates.description: Pending human-assigned (HITL) tasks in this phase. Aggregated at wave level into the top-level hitl_tasks field, which triggers reason:'hitl_required'.

status.description: 'skipped' when agent() returned null (user skipped). 'failed' when the agent threw and was dropped by parallel().

commit_sha.description: Git SHA of the commit authored by this agent in its worktree. Null/absent if no commit was made (e.g. read-only task, or task failed).

summary.description: Brief summary of what the agent did. At most 2 sentences.

reviewer_type.description: agentType of the reviewer that produced this verdict.

required_fixes.description: Present when approved is false. Each item is an actionable fix instruction for the fix-loop agent.

council_artifacts.description: Present only when reviewer_type is 'council-review'. Contains the ARC run artifact paths.

CouncilArtifacts.description: Paths to the ARC run artifacts produced by a council-review gate. All paths are relative to repo root.

run_dir.description: Path to the run directory, e.g. '.claude/skills/council-review/runs/2026-06-01-execute-plan-phase-2'.

findings_yaml.description: Path to findings.yaml within the run directory.

scorecard_json.description: Path to scorecard.json within the run directory.

risk_register_yaml.description: Path to risk_register.yaml within the run directory.

decision_record_md.description: Path to decision_record.md within the run directory.

validation_plan_md.description: Path to validation_plan.md within the run directory.

task_id.description: Task that surfaced the blocker, if applicable.
